purpose: C3 latency: PLAN.md gates 'Incremental Parse Latency' (median <0.2ms, p95 <1.0ms, p99 <5.0ms) and 'Temporal Query Latency' (<200ms at 10K edges).
verifier_and_storage_source_frozen: five source files the measured paths run through are copied byte-exact into fixture/ and sha256-pinned; none modified; latency code changes nothing under verifyci/.

incremental_parse.path: verifyci/ingestion/incremental.py IncrementalParser: parse(base) cold, then edit(byte coords)+parse(new) warm — the tree-sitter path run_ingest would take; tree edited before reparse, per tree-sitter contract.
incremental_parse.workload_file: fixture/workload.py (copy of verifyci/orchestration/scheduler.py — representative medium agent-edit target; exact bytes recorded in results.json, not assumed here)
incremental_parse.edit_script: deterministic: for i in range(N), append a same-purpose trailing comment `# v{i}` to interior line (i % 37) + 8 — pure insertion, byte coordinates computed from current source; every rep is one small insertion like a real edit, never a rewrite-all.
incremental_parse.warm_cold: cold = first full parse without old tree (reported as context baseline); warm = the 1000 edited incremental parses — gate numbers are WARM percentiles
incremental_parse.timing: time.perf_counter_ns around the parse call only; gc disabled during the sampling loop, re-enabled after; process priority untouched

temporal_query.path: verifyci/storage/graph_store.py get_entity_as_of — the valid-time primitive graph.query(asOf) delegates to. SELECT * ... logical_entity_id=? AND valid_from<=? AND (valid_until IS NULL OR valid_until>?) ORDER BY valid_from DESC LIMIT 1, backed by idx_entities_logical.
temporal_query.scale: DB built to the PLAN spec: >=10K edges. fixture-free builder: 2000 logical entities x 5 temporal versions = 10,000 entity rows; 10,000 CALLS/CONTAINS edges; timeline spread 2020-01-01..2024-01-01.
temporal_query.query_selection: deterministic seed: random logical id + as_of at mid-timeline; hit-rate recorded (queries must return a row — an all-miss benchmark measures nothing)
temporal_query.timing: per-query perf_counter_ns around execute+fetch only; connection reused, opened once outside the samples

percentiles: numpy-free: sorted samples, index = ceil(q*n)-1 for p50/p95/p99; p99 at n=1000 = 10th-largest sample

gate_classification.established_on_this_host: threshold satisfied by measured percentiles; numbers + env + source hashes recorded
gate_classification.cross_machine_claim: NOT made: latency is host-specific; reproducibility = protocol + hashes + environment, so a later host can compare, not inherit
gate_classification.no_retrofit: thresholds are from PLAN.md and were not changed after seeing results

rerun_guard: test_latency_repro re-runs the harness under VERIFYCI_LATENCY_RERUN=1 and asserts: same source hashes, same sample counts, median within +/-50% of recorded (machine variance allowance), same gate classification. It never asserts identical ns.

first_frozen_measurement.incremental_gates: median MET (34.6us << 200us); p95 NOT met (3.79ms > 1ms); p99 unstable vs its 5ms limit
first_frozen_measurement.temporal_gates: MET with ~3 orders of margin (p99 0.16ms vs 200ms limit); DB: 10,000 edges, 10,000 entity rows, 5.6MB, hit_rate 1.0
first_frozen_measurement.p99_instability_disclosure: THREE runs: p99 = 6.14, 4.54, 4.33 ms against the same 5.0ms limit - verdict flips MIS/MET/MET while p95 fails identically (~3.8ms) every run and median passes identically (~33us). The guard pins only the stable claims (median MET, p95 MIS, temporal MET); the p99 line is stored as run-variance evidence: at this threshold, a 1000-sample protocol cannot establish the gate on this host.
first_frozen_measurement.mechanism_analysis: split-half medians (31.0 -> 40.1 us) show mild cumulative growth from the monotonically-inserted comments; per-edit-line medians (19.9us at line 34 vs 4296us at line 39) show the dominant cost is edit position: tree-sitter re-lexes from the mutation to the next change point, so early-file edits re-lex a long tail. The 35us median confirms reparsing IS incremental (cold full parse is 3.7ms). This is representative-workload behavior, not a harness error: the one-shot shape preflight (incremental vs cold tree equality) passed.
first_frozen_measurement.conclusion: incremental gate NOT met (p95 3.8ms > 1ms) on this host for the rotating-position workload; temporal gate MET with massive margin. Measured; thresholds were not retuned; no source changed.
